title: Front-wheel drive on an icy hill: nose first, or in reverse? 10 deg ice: only reverse climbs, 1.92 m
description:
Front-wheel drive on an icy hill: nose first, or in reverse? The same car on the same 10 degree icy hill floors it from rest. Nose first it rolls back 0.85 m in 5 s. In reverse it climbs 1.92 m in 5 s.

Model: a 1,300 kg front-wheel-drive car, wheelbase L = 2.6 m, 60 / 40 front-to-rear static split so the centre of mass is b = 1.56 m ahead of the rear axle and h = 0.55 m up, grip mu = 0.3 on ice, a theta = 10 degree hill (all chosen); g = 9.807 m/s^2. The car starts at rest with the brakes on; at the throttle the driver floors it, so the driven front wheels spin and push uphill with the most the ice gives, mu N_front; the rear wheels roll free and push nothing. The slope and the acceleration a (uphill positive) move load onto the downhill axle:
N_front = m g cos theta (b / L) -/+ m (g sin theta + a) (h / L)
N_rear = m g cos theta - N_front
a = mu N_front / m - g sin theta
with the minus sign nose first (the front axle uphill, unloaded) and the plus sign in reverse (the front axle downhill, loaded). Solved exactly, N_front / (m g) = (b / L) cos theta / (1 +/- mu h / L): the sin terms cancel, a is constant and the car moves s = a t^2 / 2 from rest; the mass cancels too. Both runs are integrated by RK4 at 1000 steps per second for 5 s with the loads solved from the state at every stage and checked against the closed form and a half-step rerun. Real time, five runs on one clock; the picture holds after 5 s.

Measured:
- At rest with the brakes on the front axle already carries 0.5542 of the weight nose first and 0.6276 in reverse: the hill alone leans the weight onto the downhill wheels.
- Nose first (front axle uphill): wheels spinning, the front axle carries 0.5556 of the weight (7084 N), the rear 0.4292 (5472 N). The ice gives mu N_front = 1.6347 m/s^2 of push against 1.7030 m/s^2 of slope, so a = -0.0683 m/s^2: the car slides back 0.8533 m in 5 s and is moving at -0.3413 m/s, its wheels still spinning forward.
- In reverse (front axle downhill): the front axle carries 0.6309 of the weight (8044 N), the rear 0.3539 (4512 N). The push is 1.8562 m/s^2 against the same 1.7030 of slope, so a = +0.1533 m/s^2: it climbs 1.9159 m in 5 s and is moving at +0.7664 m/s.
- Steepest hill it can hold at full throttle (a = 0): tan theta* = mu b / (L + mu h) = 9.61 degrees nose first, mu b / (L - mu h) = 10.88 degrees in reverse. The window between them is 1.27 degrees wide and the 10 degree hill sits inside it, so the answer rests on the chosen grip, split and centre-of-mass height.
- Grip 0.2: both roll back (a = -0.5910 and -0.4928 m/s^2, -7.39 m and -6.16 m in 5 s; steepest 6.57 and 7.14 degrees). Grip 0.4: both climb (a = +0.4341 and +0.8292 m/s^2, +5.43 m and +10.37 m; steepest 12.48 and 14.69 degrees).
- Rear-wheel drive nose first at grip 0.3: the driven rear axle is downhill but carries only 0.4598 of the weight, a = -0.3501 m/s^2, -4.38 m in 5 s, steepest 7.30 degrees. All-wheel drive: a = +1.1944 m/s^2, +14.93 m in 5 s, steepest atan(mu) = 16.70 degrees, whatever the split.
- Checks: 23 checks against the expected numbers, 0 failed; both axle loads positive in both runs and summing to m g cos theta; RK4 within 1.6e-13 m of the closed form; a half-step rerun agrees within 1.0e-13 m.

Why: on a hill the weight leans onto the downhill wheels, and flooring it leans it further. Nose first the driving front wheels are uphill and carry only 56 percent of the weight, so the ice gives less push than the slope takes and the car slides back. In reverse the driving wheels are downhill and carry 63 percent, and that push beats the slope.

Drawing: the car 4.2 m long at one scale with a true 10 degree slope; the centre of mass is marked +0.26 m ahead of the mid-wheelbase. The driven wheel's spoke is drawn spinning at a fixed rate while the wheels spin (drawing only; the spin rate is not modelled).

Deterministic, no seed. Rerun sims/icyhill/icyhill.py with projects/icyhill/manifest.json and you get these numbers exactly.

Made end to end by an AI agent: simulation, footage, voice, music, and edit.
